# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 45 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 45 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_045_page_001.jpg

---

## Council Notes

This chapter addresses an objection that Hermas (and presumably his audience) would raise: the commandments are too hard to keep. The Shepherd's response is purely theocentric — the argument is not "you can do it if you try" but "God is powerful enough to enable you." This is a significant theological move that parallels Paul's "I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me."

The phrase "those who rule over the living and the dead" (*tous kratountas kai tous nekrous*) has puzzled commentators; it may refer to angels of death or demonic powers claiming dominion, rather than human rulers. EMET takes it as a reference to powerful human rulers; LOGOS similarly; PNEUMA suggests demonic "powers over the living and the dead."

SOPHIA retains the ambiguity of EMET/LOGOS, reading it as human rulers with possible demonic backing — consistent with Hermas's general worldview.

---

## Mandate 12, Part 2 — God's Power Enables Obedience

**45:1** He said to me: "You know that you are a servant of God and serve in his dominion, and that his power is great and incomprehensible, and that he made all things and established them out of nothing, and that he alone contains all things and is himself contained by nothing.

**45:2** Have faith therefore in him and fear him; and in your fear of him, exercise self-control. Keep these things and cast away from yourself all evil desire, and clothe yourself with every good and holy desire. For if you keep these commandments, you shall live to God."

**45:3** "Lord," I said, "strengthen me, for I have many distractions — from the world, and from the devil, and from those who rule the living and the dead, and from powerful men. For there are many diversions that carry me away." "I know," he said, "but I will be with you and will deliver you from all of them. Only keep my commandments and you will not be given over to them. Trust in God and he will deliver you."

**45:4** "I do trust him, lord," I said. "But why do you not fear him as well?" he said. "Lord," I said, "your commandments are great and good and glorious and able to save the soul of a man. But if the heart of a man has become very hard toward God and there is great weakness in him, he despairs and says in his heart: these things are too hard to keep. His heart therefore hardens and he forsakes the living God."

**45:5** "These thoughts are from the devil," he said, "who is hostile to your Lord. Do not let such thoughts enter your heart, and do not waver concerning these commandments as though you were unable to keep them. Rather, call to mind him who is able to do all things and who accomplishes all things as he wills. Through his great power and his great glory he is able to fulfill all these things. Therefore trust in God and believe in him."

---

*SOPHIA represents the consensus rendering of EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA, with rulings recorded in the Disagreement Log.*
